evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said: 'we just wanted to ask you some questions in order for us to build you an accurate code you can depend on this would take within the next five to ten minutes of your time would that be okay?' — Time frame and promise present, but phrasing is slightly off ('code' instead of 'quote') and the wait for confirmation is thin.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asked: 'What are your biggest concerns or what are the most important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — Asked before any logistics probing began.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised multiple concerns (packing/organization, furniture disassembly, not breaking things, reassembly). Rep followed up: 'I see no worries. We can definitely help you to unpack and move as well. This is something. And reassembling furniture, and appliances is also included on the hour rate.' — Rep dug into each concern raised and addressed the underlying need.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep did not reflect back or summarize what was heard. No version of 'So what I'm hearing is...' or confirmation checkback.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep confirmed: property type (two-story), bedrooms (4), additional spaces (2 downstairs living spaces, kitchen, garage, back porch, 2.5 bathrooms), parking (driveway), access concerns (none), destination (3484 sq ft, 4 bedrooms, driveway, no access issues). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Customer volunteered need; rep confirmed: 'We can definitely help you to unpack and move as well' and 'reassembling furniture, and appliances is also included on the hour rate.'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Not asked. Rep never offered a typical box count or checked for overflow items like china or book collections.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_routing: Rep correctly identified home size (2001 sq ft + 3484 sq ft, clearly ≥1800 sq ft) and offered walkthrough: 'Normally based on your home size, we do a virtual walkthrough. In that way, we will just base it on the items that we are moving. Do you have time to complete the virtual walkthrough today?' Customer not at house; rep pivoted to accept realtor video, created upload link, and scheduled follow-up after review. Call ended cleanly with next step confirmed.

top_strength: Rep identified the customer's core concern (packing/organization with four kids) early and dug into what that meant — furniture disassembly, assembly, organized placement — rather than brushing past it, and confirmed every detail needed to set up the virtual walkthrough.
coaching_note: Add an active listening summary ('So what I'm hearing is packing, disassembly, reassembly, and organized placement — did I get that?') before moving to logistics probing, and ask about box count/overflow (china, books) even on walkthrough-routed calls to help the walkthrough specialist get ready.
booking_note: Customer agreed to send photos/video for virtual walkthrough review, but no move date was locked in. Agent said 'I'll review it then I'll call you as soon as I can' - next step is assessment, not confirmed booking.
